title: Workbench layout definition
description: One named workbench layout (_data/workbench/layouts/<id>.json, REQ-007 W05/W16, ADR-016 kept by ADR-031). schema_version 4: the per-panel eligibility list is gone. A layout declares its slots (slot_id is the slot's role), the panel types it uses, a default total assignment and the default visible panel for any slot that holds more than one panel; which slot roles a panel type may occupy is computed from _data/workbench/panel-elements.json and _data/workbench/slot-schemas.json (ADR-031 decision 4, REQ-011 R12), so a `panels` entry carrying `eligible_slots` fails this schema. This schema asserts structural shape only; the relational invariants (default_assignment/default_visible_panel/grid.areas referring to real slots and panels, the assignment being total and structurally eligible, every slot_id naming a role in slot-schemas.json) are asserted directly against the parsed JSON by test/test_workbench_layout_schema.py, which JSON Schema alone cannot express.

schema_version.description: Bumped from 3 to 4 when eligible_slots was removed from panels (ADR-031 decision 10). Earlier bumps: 2 moved eligibility from the slot to the panel (REQ-007 W16); 3 renamed the slot ids to role names.

default_assignment.description: panel_id -> slot_id, a total mapping over every panel declared in `panels`; the slot must be one the panel type is structurally eligible for.

default_visible_panel.description: slot_id -> panel_id, for slots whose default assignment gives them more than one panel.
